chapter: Charleston childhood and the Jenkins Orphanage
title: Jenkins Orphanage band, white sponsors and the Jenkins family
summary: Briggs talks about how white patrons supported Mr. Jenkins and his orphanage band, rumours of Jenkins's wealth, his son's unhappiness with the treatment of the orphans, and the Patrick cousins.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: That was a period when things were getting tougher for blacks
Yes, it was pretty rough, but there were patrons who were pretty nice to the blacks.
Yes, there were. Quite a few.
In what way, I mean, they'd --

In helping them to -- in the education and everything else, (Inaudible) Education and everything else they tried to -- and that's really what helped Mr. Jenkins and the way he was sponsored and helped, you see, to organize his --
Right. In other words he was getting -- most of his support was being raised by whites?
They kept the thing going by donations, but also he was making

Right, he did make a whole lot of money. I mean that's a question I don't want to discuss. That question -- because I'm not sure. It's said that he made quite a lot of money. He was a millionaire when he died.
Because it was, -- I know that's been said. He was taking and putting some of that in his pocket.

Yes, he -- but I think it was, as far as I'm concerned, his son didn't say much when we tried to find out certain things from him, but he didn't say much -- but he was not on very good terms with his father.
Social reasons, for social reasons. Probably that had something to do with it. He did not appreciate the treatment of orphans in the band.
The son. He didn't -- he didn't appreciate -- but I learned through the two boys who worked with me that Patrick Brothers, the cousin....
Who were in the band. And Edmund Jenkins himself, was very, very familiar with those two boys.

He happened to know them because they were youngsters when he left, and I believe Patrick was -- yes, Patrick was a member of the band that came over with Jenkins when Edmund stayed to continue his musical studies.
